flags: The privacy policy does not explicitly disclose whether customer data (conversations, lead interactions, call logs) is used to train Lofty's agentic AI models. OpenAI is listed as a sub-processor, but the data flow and training purpose are unclear. This matters because AI is a primary product feature.

The vendor claims SOC 2 certification but does not specify Type I vs Type II. Type I covers the design of controls, while Type II covers their operation over a 6+ month period; these are substantively different assurance levels.

Unlike many enterprise SaaS vendors, Lofty provides no public SOC 2 audit report, trust certificate, or third-party verification link. The certification claim is stated but not independently verifiable.
22 sub-processors are listed, including OpenAI, Google Cloud, AWS, and Zendesk; however, the scope and purpose of customer data shared with each is not clearly articulated in the DPA.

Despite marketing agentic AI as a core feature and heavy use of AI agents for autonomous decision-making, Lofty holds no ISO 42001 AI governance certification. This gap may be relevant for enterprise buyers in regulated industries.

While not a healthcare product, Lofty processes contact information, communication records, and lead data that could be sensitive for certain users; no Business Associate Agreement (BAA) option appears to be available.
Data is stored exclusively in the US, with no option for EU data residency despite GDPR compliance claims. Organizations with data residency mandates cannot use Lofty.
